beats.ch01.s01.b014: Sol's feet go apart before she decides to move.

beats.ch01.s01.b026: Sol spins the dial. Static, then a warm rapid voice.
beats.ch01.s01.b028: Water over the barriers at Blackgate. I say again, water over the barriers at Blackgate. This is not the tide. Move to your upstairs floors. Do not go down.
beats.ch01.s01.b029: He's saying the barriers are gone.
beats.ch01.s01.b030: A hundred years old, built for a different river.
beats.ch01.s01.b031: Dell puts the notebook into her hands and closes her fingers around it.
beats.ch01.s01.b032: You know what a breaker does. You read a line by ear better than I ever did. That's not a kindness, it's a fact.
beats.ch01.s01.b034: Four that matter tonight. They trip, they get reset by hand, because the automatic's gone.
beats.ch01.s01.b035: Sol opens the cover. Old ink, brown at the edges, and her own pencil in the margins.
beats.ch01.s01.b036: I wrote this when I was sixteen.
beats.ch01.s01.b037: Three of them are in the book. The fourth is off every map there is, and I'm the reason.
beats.ch01.s01.b040: Not on a roof in a storm. When the three are back, ask me where it lives. Ask me on the air, so Ozzy hears it. I've kept a thing too long.
beats.ch01.s01.b041: You expect me to find a breaker that isn't on paper.
beats.ch01.s01.b042: I expect you to be the part that isn't written.

beats.ch01.s01.b044: Roof. Leave it. All of it. Just the bag.

beats.ch01.s01.b049: I'd like to have finished the boat.
beats.ch01.s01.b051: I'd like to have finished it before tonight. That's not the same thing.
beats.ch01.s02.b002: Below, the long bright string of the market district plunges end to end. Then the waterworks and the low neighborhoods, block by block. Then the tram depot. The hospital flickers twice and holds.
beats.ch01.s02.b004: That's the emergency line. Wards, lifts, blood fridge, the lights in the operating rooms. That's what we're buying time for.
beats.ch01.s02.b006: Dell gives no answer. That is the answer.
beats.ch01.s02.b007: Sol looks down at the black water where Canal Street should be.
beats.ch01.s02.b008: A city's a circuit. Everything that makes it a city is a current running through copper in the dark.
beats.ch01.s02.b010: Sol pulls a handheld radio from the bag. Static, then the warm voice, thin now, with rain on it.
beats.ch01.s02.b012: This is Ozzy Kwan in the tower on Perch Street, and I am going to stay with you. Power is down in the market and the waterworks and most of the west side. The hospital is on its emergency line.
beats.ch01.s02.b013: That line is a battery of hearts, and it does not run forever. If anyone knows a soul who can get to the grid, tell them to find Ozzy Kwan. I'll be here.
beats.ch01.s02.b015: The waterworks. Where the canal bends. You'll have to swim to the vault, more likely than wade.
beats.ch01.s02.b017: Read it by sound and touch. The water's already made the book a liar.
beats.ch01.s02.b018: Far off a crowd makes a long low sound, and the rain takes it.
beats.ch01.s02.b021: A week, and a chair that doesn't squeak, and a boat I meant to finish. The storm can't read a calendar.
beats.ch01.s02.b022: Sol stops at the roof door.
beats.ch01.s02.b023: When the three are back, ask me where the fourth lives. On the air.
beats.ch01.s02.b024: My book's a map, and the water's made the map a liar. Three in the book. One off it. One circuit.
beats.ch01.s02.b025: I'll ask you on the air.
beats.ch01.s02.b027: Sol goes down into the cold, busy water. The notebook stays dry in her coat. The dead things in the bag wait to be alive.
beats.ch01.s02.b029: The rain comes down on the dark city, and the city listens.
beats.ch02.s01.b003: I can see it's you. That's why I said far enough.
beats.ch02.s01.b004: The hospital's on its emergency line. You can hear it if—
beats.ch02.s01.b005: I'm asking what you want. Not what's happening.
beats.ch02.s01.b006: Sol plants her feet in the current.
beats.ch02.s01.b008: Course you do. Go ask somebody who likes you.
beats.ch02.s01.b009: Nobody likes me. I'm not here to be liked. It's four breakers by hand, or the hospital's line doesn't hold past morning.
beats.ch02.s01.b010: Ife turns the boat-hook a quarter turn, like a screw.
beats.ch02.s01.b014: You had a board in the training hall last spring. The one with the burnt neutral. You told the assessor I left the tester in it.
beats.ch02.s01.b015: I remember a tester and a burn.
beats.ch02.s01.b016: I was there till two in the morning fixing what you broke. I got written up. Careless. You got promising.
beats.ch02.s01.b018: The assessor's write-up doesn't hold a hospital. It doesn't hold lights on.
beats.ch02.s01.b019: Your family's on Barrow Row. That's the hospital district.
beats.ch02.s01.b021: Barrow Row runs off the hospital's transformers. When the emergency line goes, the flats go dark. Your mother's stair. The lifts. Your gran's machine.
beats.ch02.s01.b022: Ife looks off down the black street.
beats.ch02.s01.b023: Four flights and a landing and a light that's been gone since I was twelve.
beats.ch02.s01.b025: She steps into the wheelhouse. A drawer. The radio registers with a hiss.
beats.ch02.s01.b027: First casualty reports. On the east side, at the Silt Market, a roofer, Tomas Ilyich, seventy-one, fell from an upper window reaching for a neighbour's roof. Neighbours have him. They say he is alive, and they say he needs a doctor.
beats.ch02.s01.b028: And listen—the hospital district is still lit. Still lit. That is not the same as safe.
beats.ch02.s01.b029: Ife throws the line. Sol catches it against her chest, gets the loop over the bollard, hauls.
beats.ch02.s01.b030: All right. Here's what it costs, and I'll say it once.
beats.ch02.s01.b031: The tram's down in the depot with the water over her. My engine's an old diesel on its last summer. That tram carries the motors to make her new.
beats.ch02.s01.b032: So. You get me to the depot, I get first claim on the tram's salvage. I pilot, you navigate. Say yes or climb back in the water.
beats.ch02.s01.b033: Sol turns it over once, like a fitting, to see the thread.
beats.ch02.s01.b034: The tram's not one of the four. It's not on the map.
beats.ch02.s01.b035: I know it's not on the map. That's the whole point of it.
beats.ch02.s01.b036: Yes. First claim on the tram's salvage is yours. You pilot, I navigate.
beats.ch02.s01.b037: Say it with the terms in it.
beats.ch02.s01.b038: You pilot. I navigate. The tram's salvage is your first claim. And whatever's left of the night, we split.
beats.ch02.s01.b039: They shake once, hard and brief.
beats.ch02.s01.b040: And after that, we're even on the board, and I never hear the word promising again.
beats.ch02.s01.b041: Take it. I'll say it on the radio.
beats.ch02.s01.b044: A thing said on a radio belongs to everybody. This one's mine. Say it to Dell and to the hall.
beats.ch02.s01.b045: Then it's yours. To Dell and the hall.
beats.ch02.s01.b047: Ife casts off in two pulls and lets the loop pay through her hands. The engine comes up out of its mutter into a heavy knocking note.
beats.ch02.s01.b048: Read me the way, then. I can't see a street sign from here, and the signs that are left are under the water.
beats.ch02.s01.b049: Sol goes up to the bow, Dell's notebook dry inside her coat.
beats.ch02.s01.b050: The waterworks is downriver, round the bend where the canal turns. But the straight run through the market is wrong tonight.
beats.ch02.s01.b052: She closes one ear with her thumb and turns the other to the dark.
beats.ch02.s01.b053: Hear it? A feeder arcing in the water at the market. Old pipe run, modern cable pulled through it, nobody drew where. Anyone wading there tonight, the current won't ask.
beats.ch02.s01.b054: So we go round the back of the lock keeper's lane. Deeper water, but cold water. And the bridge with the chain will tell us the true channel.
beats.ch02.s01.b055: Ife comes out of the wheelhouse to look at her.
beats.ch02.s01.b056: Say that again, slower. And put your hand on the gunwale while you say it, so I know you're not making it up.
beats.ch02.s01.b057: Sol puts her hand on the gunwale and says it again.
beats.ch02.s01.b059: Hung under the arch on the keystone, and the keystone on the old pilings. High water, it drags and rings. When it rings, it rings off the true channel.
beats.ch02.s01.b061: I don't. Dell knows it, and now I've got Dell's book.
beats.ch02.s01.b062: She touches the cover once through her coat.
beats.ch02.s01.b064: Keep that dry. Both of them.
beats.ch02.s02.b002: Past the locksmith's. Now the lane.
beats.ch02.s02.b003: It's a living room. It's somebody's living room and we're driving through it.
beats.ch02.s02.b004: Stoop at eleven, railings on the left. Then the dead service pipe.
beats.ch02.s02.b006: The barge nudges a wall and grinds along it. Above, a curtain moves.
beats.ch02.s02.b008: Someone's watching us out of their upstairs like we're the weather.
beats.ch02.s02.b010: There. The chain. I hear it.
beats.ch02.s02.b013: The barge slides under the arch and the ringing passes overhead and falls behind. Ahead the lane opens into a long straight reach.
beats.ch02.s02.b016: Straight from here. The waterworks at the end of it.
beats.ch02.s02.b017: Then get up here where I can see you.
beats.ch02.s02.b018: Sol climbs to the wheelhouse. Ife keeps her eyes forward.
beats.ch02.s02.b019: One thing. You said you'd say it to Dell and the hall. What if Dell won't hear it? Man's retiring in a week and he's off his map tonight, by the sound of you.
beats.ch02.s02.b021: That's not an answer, that's a hope.
beats.ch02.s02.b022: He gave me his book and his bag and told me to ask him the hard questions on the air. A man who does that will hear a word in a room.
beats.ch02.s02.b024: Keep that radio up. I want to know what the man says next.
beats.ch02.s02.b025: Ozzy's voice comes out of the little set, thin but steady.
beats.ch02.s02.b026: Still lit. Write it down. Say it over your stairs. The hospital is still lit.
beats.ch02.s02.b027: The barge pushes a slow white wrinkle ahead of it, and the wrinkle goes out into the black and is gone.
beats.ch03.s01.b002: Houses on your left are nine and eleven. Stoop at eleven. Iron railings.
beats.ch03.s01.b005: The bow swings a hand's width. Iron scrapes wood, complains, and is gone.
beats.ch03.s01.b006: Pipe on the right. Hundred-year-old service run. Hear it? Not a hum. A leak. On nothing.
beats.ch03.s01.b008: Meaning it's dead. It can't hurt us. Leave it alone.
beats.ch03.s01.b009: There's a cable in that wall three feet up. Dead too. Cut at the junction where the lane bends. Somebody did that right.
beats.ch03.s01.b010: Somebody did that sometime. Kick the stern off that stoop.
beats.ch03.s02.b004: When it rings, it rings off the true channel. Best sound all night.
beats.ch03.s02.b006: The barge comes in on a patient quarter turn. The chain goes by on the left, ringing.
beats.ch03.s02.b007: Beyond the arch the water opens into a long straight reach. Low at the end of it, huddled and dark, the waterworks.
beats.ch03.s02.b010: Smell that? Wet stone. Old iron. Under it, a solder iron left on.
beats.ch03.s02.b012: That's the fault. Dock us anywhere. Water's over the loading steps, but there's a platform inside the arch.
beats.ch03.s03.b002: Not a hum. A stutter. Mosquito at a window.
beats.ch03.s03.b003: Sol walks her palm down the cold wall. Below her hand the cold has a shape. Out in the middle of the floor, a wrong bathwater warmth.
beats.ch03.s03.b004: Fault's on the vault floor. East side, under the second bay. Live in the water, and the water carries it round like a rumor up a stairwell.
beats.ch03.s03.b007: The needle sits at nothing. She moves the lead a yard. Nothing. A yard toward the warm place, and the needle kicks once, a nervous twitch.
beats.ch03.s03.b009: Two yards from here it bites. Past that it's the grave.
beats.ch03.s03.b010: So we don't go past that.
beats.ch03.s03.b011: No. I go down under it and come up under the vault hatch and do it by touch.
beats.ch03.s03.b013: And if you don't come up?
beats.ch03.s03.b014: Then don't come in after me. Keep the engine running and the radio on.
beats.ch03.s03.b016: If I don't come up, you take the barge to Dell at the grid. You tell him the first one's done, which it will be. Then you get the hospital the rest of the way.
beats.ch03.s03.b017: And you take the tram's salvage and you don't think about it twice.
beats.ch03.s03.b018: If you don't come up, I'm not going to the tram depot for salvage. I'm going to Barrow Row for my mother.
beats.ch03.s03.b020: Sol puts the tester away and takes a breath and goes down.
beats.ch03.s03.b021: Under the water it is a low roar and then a beat of pressure. Cold at the top, colder at the bottom.
beats.ch03.s03.b022: Sol counts the pressure beats to keep herself slow. One. Two. The heat comes before she expects it, a warm cloud against her face, tasting of a battery's mouth.
beats.ch03.s03.b023: She goes still and lets the current carry her around it instead of through it.
beats.ch03.s03.b024: Her fingers find the hatch handle. The handle is hot. She does not let it stop her. Her thumb crosses the housing and finds the breaker body: cast, old, worn, the lever up.
beats.ch03.s03.b025: The lever is up because it tripped. All she has to do is pull it down. It fights her.
beats.ch03.s03.b026: Sol braces her shoulder on the housing and drags the lever an inch, another inch, silt grating in the mechanism.
beats.ch03.s03.b027: The lever goes home with a clack she feels through her jaw rather than hears through the water.
beats.ch03.s03.b028: The current changes. The warm cloud goes cool. The stutter above her stops as if a door opened and let the rumor out.
beats.ch03.s03.b031: The maintenance lamp over the arch was dead. Now it glows a sickly orange, and stays on.
beats.ch03.s03.b035: Sol shakes the handheld out. It comes back on with a burr in it.
beats.ch03.s03.b036: —repeat, the hospital district is holding. Backup generators have come in. The wards are steady, the lifts are running, and the blood fridge is holding cold.
beats.ch03.s03.b037: I want you to hear that cold. Cold blood is a good sign. It means the line has bought time.
beats.ch03.s03.b038: And whoever in the waterworks district just got the pumps back up, the lamps are coming on in the low streets. If that was you, thank you.
beats.ch03.s03.b039: But a lit lamp is not a dry street. Stay up.
beats.ch03.s03.b040: Sol sits on the ledge with her boots in the water and lets the small thing in her chest go quiet.
beats.ch03.s04.b002: Sol puts the torch on the reach. A signpost. A mailbox under water. A lamp green with weed.
beats.ch03.s04.b003: Then, further right, the roof. There is a person on the roof.
beats.ch03.s04.b005: A woman in an oversized raincoat pulls at a supply crate on wet slate. The crate sits in the gutter, the water lapping its corner, and she is not winning.
beats.ch03.s04.b006: Don't. I know that voice. I've been that voice. That's a woman doing sums.
beats.ch03.s04.b007: There's a chimney stack left of her.
beats.ch03.s04.b008: Then she's got a line and we've got a crate. You're learning, promising.
beats.ch03.s04.b011: Sol gets her feet under her in the bow. Twenty yards of black water to the roof. The coil is old and stiff and does not want to go.
beats.ch03.s04.b012: She loops half the line in the bottom of the bow, takes the rest in her left hand, puts her right hand through it, and lets the coil's own bulk carry it.
beats.ch03.s04.b013: The line goes up and out, comes down across the gutter, and goes into the water a yard short.
beats.ch03.s04.b016: The second throw goes high and wide. The woman gets a hand to it, then both, and wraps it twice.
beats.ch03.s04.b018: Tie it to the chimney! Not the pot, the stack itself! Two rounds and a knot you can't argue with!
beats.ch03.s04.b019: The stack holds. Haul when she ties!
beats.ch03.s04.b020: The woman works with her whole body. Sol takes two turns round the bollard and lets Ife have the engine and pay it out slow.
beats.ch03.s04.b021: The line comes up out of the water, stands straight and singing, and the crate slides over the ridge and stops against the chimney.
beats.ch03.s04.b024: Ife's jaw works. She does not answer.
beats.ch03.s04.b025: Ife Aduba! Barge Aduba, out of Canal Street!
beats.ch03.s04.b026: Tell your block a roofer fell in the market, and the market needs a doctor!
beats.ch03.s04.b028: She points up at the sky, then hard at the dark where Barrow Row lies. Then she sits down with her child and her dry crate.
beats.ch03.s04.b030: Ife puts the engine in gear. The reach opens ahead.
beats.ch03.s04.b031: That's forty feet of my good line gone. I want it back before the night's out.
beats.ch03.s04.b033: She pointed. Over toward the market.
beats.ch03.s04.b035: I think she's got a doctor.
beats.ch03.s04.b036: Then let's get the market's breaker and leave the doctor to it.
beats.ch03.s04.b037: Two down and two to go. Tell me the way.
beats.ch03.s04.b039: The reach runs straight to the market. The market's a square with streets off it like spokes. The hub of the wheel is where the second breaker lives.
beats.ch03.s04.b040: We'll want the winch for the housing, and the bolt set won't want to turn.
beats.ch03.s04.b041: Keep your hand on that rail while you say it.
beats.ch03.s04.b042: Sol keeps her hand there. The barge goes on down the reach into the dark.
beats.ch03.s04.b043: The hospital district is still lit. Say it over your stairs. Still lit.
beats.ch03.s04.b044: Waterworks done. Market next. Depot after.
beats.ch03.s04.b045: Sol closes her eyes and feels the river go under the hull, and puts her hand on the bag of dead things.
beats.ch03.s04.b046: Then the fourth one. The one that's off the map.
beats.ch04.s01.b002: Left. There's a car under us on the right. Take it left.
beats.ch04.s01.b004: The barge noses past the drowned car into the square. Sol keeps the torch low and calls the way a foot at a time.
beats.ch04.s01.b005: Somebody left that lamp burning for us. That's a landmark.
beats.ch04.s01.b006: Or somebody's letting the oil down slow in a cup.
beats.ch04.s01.b007: The hub's in the middle. Where?
beats.ch04.s01.b008: Sol opens the notebook under the torch. The market page shows the wheel and its spokes and a little square at the hub, with Dell's old shorthand beside it.
beats.ch04.s01.b009: Sol runs her thumb along the smudge and gets the word back: CONTACT.
beats.ch04.s01.b010: Mind the contact. That's the word.
beats.ch04.s01.b012: Meaning the housing's live somewhere it shouldn't be. Good to know before I put my hands in.
beats.ch04.s02.b002: It's ringing. Like a bell with a crack in it.
beats.ch04.s02.b003: That cap's not bolted. It's been got at.
beats.ch04.s02.b005: People. There's a whole dark city out there and copper buys things.
beats.ch04.s02.b006: Sol lifts the cap. It comes up with the housing riding with it, loosened, half out, up wrong. The cast body has a gouged hollow where a bolt and its iron have gone. A copper lug hangs out like a tongue, burnt black at the tip.
beats.ch04.s02.b008: Tell me what I'm looking at.
beats.ch04.s02.b009: Somebody had it half out with a wrench. Had that lug off and back on wrong. It heated and it burnt, the water got it, and the fault tripped it.
beats.ch04.s02.b010: Sol draws her finger above the gouge without touching it.
